2020_146_022520bdmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting of February 25, 2020, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Contents run from recognitions and the January 2020 minutes through the December 2019 Treasurer's Report with unaudited July 1 - December 31, 2019 fund statements, reports on enrollment projections and Schools of Choice, and ten business bid awards. Total disbursements in the period were $14,934,788.68. The largest award before the Board is $2,117,078.78 for site construction and site electrical work at five buildings, followed by $1,645,048.50 for the Niles Relocation and Troy Union lift project.

**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, 7:00 p.m., February 25, 2020, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district phone 248.823.4000; cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** New trustee Mrs. Vital Anne (Troy resident 16 years, master's degree in mechanical engineering, more than 25 years of engineering experience); twelve Fall 2019 All-State athletes; Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal of International Academy-East, named 2020 Michigan ASTA Administrator of the Year; a resolution naming February Principal Appreciation Month.

**Consent agenda.** January 7, 2020 Workshop minutes (6:02 p.m. to 9:47 p.m., Mr. Gottlieb absent), January 21, 2020 Organizational & Regular Meeting minutes, and the December 2019 Treasurer's Report. The January 21 meeting adopted resolutions 20-001 through 20-016: Schmidt President, Dr. Wilson Vice President, Mr. Hauff Secretary through December 31, 2020; Rick L. West appointed Treasurer for January-December 2020; depositories and investments per Board Policy 5000.06 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code; 2020 legal counsel Clark Hill PLC, Collins & Blaha P.C., Lusk Albertson, Thrun Law Firm P.C. and Beier Howlett P.C.; Bid Pack #26 re-bid awards of $187,518.00 plus $15,001.44 contingency, total $202,519.44; a Gorno Ford vehicle purchase of $143,339.00 (Yes 5; No 1 - Gottlieb; No 1 - Hammond). Trustee Paula Fleming was honored for more than 19 years of service.

**Enrollment (7.A).** Plante Moran Cresa update presented by Dr. Machesky: district median age of householder 42.1, 25,312 households, 18,583 families, 11,603 households with school age children, 45.8% of households with children, 13,017 enrolled school-aged children, 89.96% in public K-12. Projection table shows birth year 2013, births 13,445, K% of births 6.23%, K-12 enrollment 12,548, difference -8, growth -0.06%, total 13,085. Recommendation: flat enrollment year-over-year for budget and planning.

**Schools of Choice (7.B-7.D).** Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park closed to open enrollment; Athens and Troy High closed except for not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area. Section 105/105c resolution accepts 30 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 13 total sixth through eighth grade nonresident students for 2020-2021.

**Identification.** Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting agenda packet for February 25, 2020, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; administrative address 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** New appointed trustee Mrs. Vital Anne was sworn in before the meeting; she and her husband Siva have lived in Troy 16 years, and she holds a master's degree in mechanical engineering with more than 25 years of engineering experience. Mr. Fulcher read the Fall 2019 All-State athletes: Paige Anderson (Troy High cross country, coach Matt Richardson), Gabe Brown (Athens boys tennis, Andrew Shipp), Brennan Cimpeanu, Jagan Nallani, Rishi Shetty and Andrew Wang (Troy High boys tennis, Brian Miska), Ahmad Dakrouni and Rafael Khoury (Troy High boys soccer, Jim Stachura), Olivia Hemmila (Athens girls golf, Dan Cooper), and Jason Kemp, Andri Myftari and T J Renaud (Athens boys soccer, Todd Heugh). The Mission Moment honored Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal of International Academy-East, as the 2020 Michigan ASTA Administrator of the Year, presented at the Michigan Music Conference in Grand Rapids in January, with Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction Christine DiPilato speaking to the nomination. A resolution recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy.

**Consent agenda and minutes.** Items A-C were the January 7, 2020 Board Workshop minutes, the January 21, 2020 Organizational & Regular Meeting minutes, and the Treasurer's Report - December 2019. The January 7 workshop was called to order at 6:02 p.m. by President Schmidt and adjourned at 9:47 p.m.; present were Schmidt, Fleming, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, with Mr. Gottlieb absent, Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, West, Carson, Griffor and Harris, plus Steve Brandimore of Safe-Ed and two TMP Architecture representatives; topics included the Niles relocation, Bid Pack #26 re-bid pool equipment, tile and scaffolding, an operations vehicle purchase, security protocol, communications strategy and committee assignments. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

The January 21, 2020 organizational and regular meeting convened at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned at 9:22 p.m., with all seven trustees, four high school student representatives, roughly 25 audience members, Troy Mayor Ethan Baker and State Representative Padma Kuppa present. Resolutions 20-001 through 20-016 were adopted: Schmidt acting chairperson and then President through December 31, 2020 (roll call 7-0); Dr. Wilson Vice President and Mr. Hauff Secretary through December 31, 2020 (both 7-0); Judy Holmes appointed temporary secretary and designated to post meeting notices; Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2020; a fund depositories and investments resolution naming Bank of America, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus) managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank and PNC Bank, with checks bearing the facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West or, in emergencies, the handwritten signature of West or Superintendent Richard M. Machesky on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America, PNC accounts for Troy Career Center expenses, and a Comerica account for flexible spending claims paid by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc.; investments are made under Board Policy 5000.06 and funds may be combined for investments authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Legal counsel designated for calendar 2020: Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. The Superintendent was designated Deputy Secretary. Personnel resolution 20-012 approved new hires Alexia Mancilla-Jackson, Jennifer Kuntz, Laura Stedman and Claire Reid. Resolution 20-013 awarded Bid Pack #26 Re-Bid Pool, Tile and Scaffolding to Contrast Mechanical (scaffolding) $78,000.00 and Southeastern Tile (tiles) $109,518.00, total contract awards $187,518.00, contingency $15,001.44, total $202,519.44, as an expenditure of the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds and the Sinking Fund. Resolution 20-014 awarded an operations vehicle purchase to Gorno Ford for $143,339.00 from the 2019-2020 General Fund, Yes 5, No 1 - Gottlieb, No 1 - Hammond. Resolution 20-015 approved Mr. Schmidt's attendance at the National Equity Project Conference in Itasca, Illinois, February 26-29, 2020. January recognitions also covered the Michigan Arctic Grayling Initiative documentary by Athens TV students and teacher Adam Burns, Kris Griffor's 2020 National Excellence in Literacy Leadership Award, and retiring trustee Paula Fleming, honored with City of Troy and State of Michigan proclamations and a crystal award for more than 19 years of service.

**7.A Enrollment Projections.** Report by Dr. Machesky using Plante Moran Cresa analysis, slide deck 'Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Update - February 25, 2020'; no action required. PMC's process covers demographic growth, GIS, US Census Bureau data, Core Base Statistical Area, primary area, county and state comparisons and Cohort Survival DS 4061. District demographics: median age of householder 42.1; 25,312 households; 18,583 families; 11,603 households with school age children; 45.8% of households with children; 13,017 enrolled school-aged children; public PK 43.24% and private PK 56.76%; public K-12 89.96% and private K-12 10.04%. City of Troy demographics: median age of householder 53.8; 30,703 households; 22,443 families; trend of -0.6% for ages 0-5, 0.6% for ages 6-11 and -0.3% for ages 12-17. The district-wide projection table lists birth year 2013, births 13,445, K% of births 6.23%, K-12 enrollment 12,548, difference -8, growth -0.06% and total 13,085. Recommendation: flat enrollment year-over-year for budget and planning purposes.

**7.B-7.D Schools of Choice.** Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park Schools are closed to open enrollment for 2020-2021; Athens and Troy High are also closed except for not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students residing in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens, with applications accepted during a two-week window in March, and siblings currently in grades 9-11 allowed to remain. Kris Griffor and Christine DiPilato presented the Section 105 and 105c report first shared at the February 11 workshop. Elementary Schools of Choice counts for 2019-2020 total 377 SOC and 5,077 non-SOC students, 6.91% and -1.14% change, ranging from Hill Elementary 72 SOC (19.51%) to Schroeder 1 (0.19%); non-SOC enrollment by grade totals 11,775. Application history since 2006-2007 totals 1,005 kindergarten and 314 first grade openings advertised, 1,868 and 568 applications and 1,035 and 267 students enrolled. Projected sibling preference placements are 30 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 13 middle school; the February 11, 2020 memorandum recommends accepting those numbers using Plante Moran Cresa projections, with additional students possible in the third week of August. The 7.D resolution, under Section 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepts a Limited Schools of Choice program of 30 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 13 total sixth through eighth grade nonresident students, with middle school seats at Baker, Larson and Smith.

**7.E Media 2.0 Update.** Kris Griffor presented 'Maker Centered Learning, Computer Science, & Design Thinking,' naming stakeholders Lauren Henderson and Sarah Glasser (Hamilton), Ruba Alexander and Mike Cottone (Troy Union), Matt Jansen and Lori Kostrzewa (Wass), Patrick Werner and Melanie Morey (Barnard); book studies of Maker Centered Learning and Launch; visits to Oakland Schools STEM Coaches, Rochester Delta Kelly Media Center, the Oakland Schools Coding Institute, the Smith Middle School Creation Lab and MACUL; and Harvard Project Zero coursework.

Business awards.** 8.A Niles Relocation Bid (RFP 9902, Bid Pack 29, memo from Rob Carson to Rick West dated February 6, 2020): DKI, Inc. demolition $46,700.00; Advanced Building Group general trades $503,200.00; Conventional Carpet flooring $177,900.00; General Painting $38,600.00; FCI casework/millwork $160,000.00; Contrast Mechanical $189,000.00; MCMI temperature controls $81,100.00; Ecker electrical $312,608.00; total contract awards $1,509,108.00; contingency $135,940.50; total $1,645,048.50, split as Niles $1,473,003.00 and the Troy Union ADA lift $172,045.50, funded from the 2016, 2019 and 2020 Capital Projects Funds. 8.B Network cabling for the former ITT Building (RFP 9898, eight proposals opened January 27, 2020, reviewed by Beth Soggs and Convergent Technology Partners): MOSS revised qualified bid $37,944.21 plus about 5% contingency $1,897.00, award $39,841.21 from the 2020 Capital Projects Fund; letter signed Eric Helsel, RCDD/OSP/RTPM. 8.C Site work (RFP 9895, Bid Pack 28, Barton Malow letter of January 14, 2020 signed Christa Amalio): MHM Construction site electrical $104,617.00 and Asphalt Specialists Inc. sitework $1,820,000.00, contract awards $1,924,617.00, contingency $192,461.70, total $2,117,078.70 in the attachments and $2,117,078.78 in the resolution, covering Schroeder and Hill Elementary, Athens and Troy High and International Academy East. 8.D Flooring (RFP 9905): Conventional Carpet Inc. $849,499.00, Diamond Shine Concrete and Stone Polishing $49,960.00 and $35,000.00 contingency, total $934,459.00, with work commencing April 3, 2020 and classroom completion by August 8, 2020. 8.E Bid Pack #26A pool equipment (RFP 9896): B&B Pools Inc. $245,750.00 with alternate P2 and removal of UV and anchors, contingency $12,287.50, total $258,037.50 for the Athens High School natatorium. 8.F Bus purchase: seven end-of-life buses replaced through the MSBO School Bus Purchasing Program, awarded to Hoekstra Transportation at $732,136.00 against Holland $749,647.00 and Midwest Transit $756,293.00; a February 3, 2020 letter from Steve Coulter notes Thomas Built Jouley EV pilots with Ann Arbor and Roseville, DTE and Proterra, Volkswagon Mitigation funds covering 70% and total cost of approximately $360,000 per bus. 8.G Services Board Room audio video upgrade (RFP 9897, six proposals opened January 14, 2020): MOSS $60,379.45 plus contingency $3,019.00, award $63,398.45, using a Crestron DMPS 350-C and CP3 processor. 8.H TCCHS Smart Displays: 10 aging displays replaced with 75-inch SMART Board interactive monitors from VSC off the REMC bid, $44,525.54, VSC estimate 17405 dated 1/7/2020. 8.I Asbestos abatement (RFP 9904, NOVA Environmental letter of February 5, 2020 signed Lisa Whitton): BDS Environmental / Building Decommission Services LLC $294,000.00 plus 5% contingency, award $308,700.00, covering Smith, Larson and Boulan Park Middle Schools, Hill, Costello, Wattles and Barnard Elementary and Athens High. 8.J iPad purchase: 1050 10.2-inch iPads with Logitech keyboard cases from Apple Computers for $367,500.00, prompted by a DRC error over the iPad Air's lack of 2 GB of RAM affecting WIDA ACCESS listening and MSTEP testing for 7th and 8th grades, to be ready by April 13th.
